title: Total structural query probability and average cost
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index type. Suppose the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ have a basis indexed by $\iota$ that contains the constant-one function at a distinguished index and is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For every natural number $n$ and every finite-alphabet decision tree on all $n$ coordinates, the sum of its structural query probabilities over the coordinates equals its expected query count when the input coordinates are independent with common law $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: π is a probability mass function on Ω
ι is finite and nonempty with decidable equality
A real basis of functions on Ω indexed by ι, with a distinguished constant-one vector and π-weighted orthonormality
A finite-alphabet decision tree on all n coordinates
